# My Impression of Keigo Higashino
The first work by Keigo Higashino that I read was probably *The Miracles of the Namiya General Store*.

I remember it was when I was in elementary school. I was spending my summer vacation at my cousin’s house, and since there were no phones to play with back then, I had no choice but to read. As it happened, there was a copy of *The Miracles of the Namiya General Store* there. Judging solely by the title, I thought it would be a light, slice-of-life kind of book. It turned out to be quite fascinating. The redemption brought about through letters sent across time left a deep impression on me, and I remembered the author.

The next time I encountered his work was in my second year of high school.

At the time, people in our dormitory started passing around *Journey Under the Midnight Sun*. I remember that at least three of us read it on the same Kindle. We were genuinely so engrossed that we barely ate or slept—it was almost as intense as binge-watching *Breaking Bad*. BTW, even when I read online novels, I was never as enthusiastic as I was with this one. When it was my turn to read it, I would basically finish my homework as quickly as possible during self-study periods and then sneak a look, read while eating, and keep reading even after the dormitory lights had been turned off (thank goodness for this backlit Kindle). It was my first time reading a mystery novel with such mature subject matter. Although it was dark, it also had a certain sense of realism, and the way the main plot progressed through the alternating perspectives of the male and female leads was quite interesting. More importantly, the story was full of twists and turns, and it was very difficult to guess who the killer was. The most heartbreaking part was that Ryoji Kirihara ultimately protected Yukiho by taking his own life, only for Yukiho to say expressionlessly, “I don’t know this person at all.”

The next time I encountered “Yukiho” was in *The Phantom Night*. This story wasn’t as compelling as *Journey Under the Midnight Sun*, though it was still fairly decent. The ending of *The Phantom Night* was also very similar to that of *Journey Under the Midnight Sun*: the male protagonist eventually discovers that the female protagonist has been deceiving and using him all along, but in the end, he still takes his own life to protect her, allowing her to escape without suspicion.

I won’t go into all his other books one by one. The image below shows the works by Keigo Higashino that I’ve read.
![Works by Keigo Higashino that I’ve read|475](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20260808043442545.png)


Keigo Higashino was a great writer. I’m grateful to him for enabling someone like me, who isn’t accustomed to reading, to concentrate and finish an entire book. I’m also grateful for the stories he created, which stay with you long after you’ve finished them.

R.I.P.

# 我對東野圭吾的印象
我第一次閱讀東野圭吾的作品，應該是他的《解憂雜貨店》。

我記得那時候還在國小，暑假在表姐家玩。那時沒有手機可以玩，於是只能看書了，剛好有一本《解憂雜貨店》。單從書名來看，我以為是日常休閒類型的書呢。這本書相當精彩，透過跨越時空的信件實現救贖，也讓我記住了這位作者。

下一次再相見就是高二了。

當時我們宿舍開始傳閱《白夜行》，我記得至少有三個人是用那台 Kindle 看完《白夜行》的。當時真的是廢寢忘食，跟追《絕命毒師》有得一比。順帶一提，我追網路小說都沒有追這本那麼積極。輪到我看的時候，我基本上就是自習課抓緊時間寫完作業後開始偷偷看、邊吃飯邊看，寢室熄燈了也繼續看（感謝這款有背光的 Kindle）。這是我第一次看這種尺度有點大的懸疑小說，雖然黑暗，卻又有一種真實感，而且男女雙視角的主線推進也滿有意思的。更重要的是，劇情確實相當跌宕起伏，凶手很難猜。最讓人意難平的是，桐原亮司最後透過自殺保護了雪穗，雪穗居然能面無表情地說出：「我完全不認識這個人。」

後來再次見到「雪穗」就是在《幻夜》中了。這個故事寫得沒有《白夜行》精彩，也算差強人意吧。《幻夜》的結局也和《白夜行》很像，男主角最後知道了女主角一直在欺騙和利用自己，但是最後他還是為了保護女主角而自殺，讓女主角清白脫身。

其他書就不一一贅述了，下面圖中是我看過的東野圭吾作品。
![看過的東野圭吾作品|475](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20260808043442545.png)


東野圭吾是一位偉大的作家，感謝他讓我這個不習慣看書的人也能集中精神讀完一本完整的書，也感謝他創作的故事讓人回味無窮。

R.I.P.

title: Building a Personal Website with Cloudflare
description: "Site architecture overview: two Workers, one SQL database, and one object storage service"
createdAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z

tags:

## Quotation

My website runs on two Cloudflare Workers, an SQL database, and object storage. Comments, likes, and view counts update in real time; my book, movie, and music collections have their own admin dashboard, and my music rankings sync automatically every night at midnight. Apart from the domain, everything else on the bill costs virtually nothing.

This article describes its architecture.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  V[访客浏览器] --> D[DNS / 优选 CNAME]
  D --> E[入口 Worker]
  E -->|Service Binding| A[Astro SSR Worker]
  A --> S[静态资源]
  A --> Q[(D1 数据库)]
  A --> R[(R2 对象存储)]
  A --> X[外部 API]

  C[Cloudflare Access] -.保护后台.-> E
  K[Cron] -.每日定时同步.-> A
```
## A Single Request's Path

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as 浏览器
  participant E as 入口 Worker
  participant A as Astro SSR Worker
  participant D1 as D1 / R2

  B->>E: HTTPS 请求
  E->>A: 内部调用（Service Binding）
  alt 静态资源
    A-->>E: 直接返回带哈希的 CSS / JS / 图片
  else 页面或 API
    A->>D1: 查询或写入
    D1-->>A: 结果
    A-->>E: HTML / JSON
  end
  E-->>B: 补上安全响应头后返回
```

## Database Design

D1 is Cloudflare’s managed SQLite database, used to store structured data such as comments, likes, view counts, and metadata for books, films, and music in your collection.

R2 stores all images: illustrations in articles and collection covers. The main reason I chose it is that egress traffic is free—bandwidth charges are the bane of image hosting. R2 stores only the files; the metadata for those files lives in D1, and the two are linked by object key.
## Image Pipeline

I write articles in Obsidian. The moment I paste an image, the image-hosting plugin uploads it directly to R2, leaving a URL in the Markdown. There are no image binary files anywhere in the repository, so the Git history never bloats.

At build time, the script generates multiple AVIF and WebP variants at several widths for each image the first time it appears (640 / 1280 / 1920), uploads them to the same directory in R2, and records the mapping in a manifest. When rendered, the URL in the Markdown remains unchanged, but the resulting HTML contains a complete `<picture>` element: the browser selects the smallest file sufficient for the viewport and pixel density, the first image in the article loads at high priority, and the rest are lazy-loaded. The original image URL always remains valid as a fallback.

## Little Money-Saving Tricks

>If your site is a purely static blog, Astro and static hosting are all you need—no Workers required.

If you need comments, an admin panel, or scheduled tasks, D1 plus an SSR Worker is a relatively low-cost option.

### Worker
Requests for static assets don’t execute any code or count toward Workers’ 100,000 free requests per day. CSS, JavaScript, fonts, and local images all fall into this category, so they’re free and unlimited. The only things that actually consume the daily allowance of 100,000 free requests are HTML rendering and API calls that require code to run.

So I keep as many requests as possible at the static layer. Only routes that require dynamic processing are configured to pass through a Worker first. This keeps request usage largely within the free-tier limits.

### D1
Keep an eye on D1 row reads. The free tier includes 5 million rows per day, but this counts rows scanned, not rows returned. A query that returns 20 comments could count tens of thousands of rows if it scans the entire table instead of using an index. Indexing commonly filtered fields and paginating lists can help you make the most of D1’s free tier.

###  A Note on Free-Tier Limits
The claim of zero cost here needs a qualification: excluding the domain name, the bill is approximately zero as long as traffic and data usage stay within the free tier. The specific allowances are (July 2026):

| Item           | Free allowance               |
| ------------ | ------------------ |
| Dynamic Worker requests | 100,000/day, shared across the account       |
| Static asset requests       | Free, unlimited             |
| D1           | 5 million row reads/day, 100,000 row writes/day |
| R2           | 10 GB of storage, free egress traffic    |

Note that 100,000 requests is the free daily limit for your entire account, not 100,000 per Worker.

Important: D1 charges based on rows scanned, so queries without indexes can make your bill skyrocket.

## Accelerating Access from Mainland China

Cloudflare’s default entry point uses Anycast, with routing determined by BGP, which isn’t always ideal for China’s three major telecom carriers. The same site may load quickly on China Telecom, while China Mobile users may experience detours and packet loss during the evening rush. My approach is to use an optimized CNAME: point my domain’s CNAME record to a hostname that continuously measures performance and updates its DNS responses.

Once traffic enters the site, speed depends on layered caching; the rules are based on how frequently each type of content changes:
- CSS/JS/fonts with content hashes: cache for one year
- HTML: `no-cache`, re-verify each time to ensure the latest code is being used
- Dynamic APIs such as comments and statistics: cache at the edge for 15 seconds; write requests always use `no-store`.
- The GitHub contribution graph is cached for 6 hours, while WakaTime data is cached for 15 minutes.

title: 基於 Cloudflare 建置個人網站
description: 此站架構介紹：兩個 Worker、一個 SQL 資料庫、一個物件儲存空間
createdAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z
updatedAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z

## 引文

我的這個網站運行著兩個 Cloudflare Worker、一個 SQL 資料庫和一個物件儲存服務。留言、按讚和瀏覽量都是即時的，書籍、電影與音樂收藏有自己的管理後台，聽歌排行每天凌晨自動同步。至於帳單，除了網域名稱之外，其他成本幾乎等於零。

本文介紹其架構

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  V[访客浏览器] --> D[DNS / 优选 CNAME]
  D --> E[入口 Worker]
  E -->|Service Binding| A[Astro SSR Worker]
  A --> S[静态资源]
  A --> Q[(D1 数据库)]
  A --> R[(R2 对象存储)]
  A --> X[外部 API]

  C[Cloudflare Access] -.保护后台.-> E
  K[Cron] -.每日定时同步.-> A
```
## 單一請求鏈路

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as 浏览器
  participant E as 入口 Worker
  participant A as Astro SSR Worker
  participant D1 as D1 / R2

  B->>E: HTTPS 请求
  E->>A: 内部调用（Service Binding）
  alt 静态资源
    A-->>E: 直接返回带哈希的 CSS / JS / 图片
  else 页面或 API
    A->>D1: 查询或写入
    D1-->>A: 结果
    A-->>E: HTML / JSON
  end
  E-->>B: 补上安全响应头后返回
```

## 資料庫設計

D1 是 Cloudflare 託管的 SQLite 資料庫，用來儲存結構化資料：留言、按讚、瀏覽量、書影音收藏的中繼資料等等。

R2 儲存所有圖片：內文插圖、收藏封面。選它的主要原因是出口流量免費，圖床最怕的就是流量費。R2 只儲存檔案，而與這些檔案對應的中繼資料在 D1 裡，兩邊透過物件鍵相互關聯。
## 圖片處理流程

我在 Obsidian 裡寫文章，貼上圖片的瞬間，圖床外掛就直接把它傳到 R2，Markdown 裡留下的是一個線上 URL。儲存庫裡從頭到尾都沒有圖片二進位檔案，git 歷史不會膨脹。

建置時，腳本會為每張首次出現的圖片產生 AVIF 和 WebP 的多個寬度版本（640 / 1280 / 1920），傳回 R2 的同一個目錄，並將對應關係寫入 manifest。渲染時，Markdown 裡的那個 URL 不變，輸出的 HTML 卻是完整的 `<picture>`：瀏覽器會依據視窗大小和像素密度，挑選最小且足夠的檔案，內文第一張圖片以高優先權載入，其餘圖片則延遲載入。原圖 URL 永遠有效，作為備援。

## 省錢小撇步

>如果你的網站是純靜態部落格，Astro 加上靜態資源託管就夠了，連一個 Worker 都不需要。  
如果需要留言、後台和定時任務，D1 加上 SSR Worker 的成本比較低。

### Worker
命中靜態資源的請求不會執行程式碼，也不會計入 Workers 每天 10 萬次的免費請求額度。CSS、JS、字型、本機圖片都屬於這類，免費且不限量。真正會消耗每天 10 萬次免費額度的，只有需要執行程式碼的 HTML 渲染和 API 呼叫。

所以我讓盡可能多的請求停留在靜態層。只有必須動態處理的路徑，才設定為先經過 Worker。這樣請求用量基本上都在免費額度範圍內。

### D1
留意 D1 的行讀取量。D1 每天提供 500 萬行的免費額度，但計算的是掃描行數，而不是回傳行數。一個回傳 20 則留言的查詢，如果沒有使用索引而掃描整張表，計入的可能是幾萬行。為常用的篩選欄位建立索引，並對清單進行分頁，這些最佳化能最大限度地利用 D1 的免費額度。

###  注意免費額度限制
這裡所說的零成本需要加上限制條件：除網域費用外，只要流量和資料量都在免費額度內，帳單就約等於零。具體額度如下（2026 年 7 月）：

| 項目           | 免費額度               |
| ------------ | ------------------ |
| Workers 動態請求 | 10 萬次/天，帳戶共用       |
| 靜態資源請求       | 免費，不限量             |
| D1           | 500 萬行讀取/天，10 萬行寫入/天 |
| R2           | 10 GB 儲存空間，出口流量免費    |

注意，10 萬次是整個帳戶每天的免費上限，不是每個 Worker 各有 10 萬次。

特別注意：D1 依掃描的資料列數計費，未使用索引的查詢會讓帳單直接爆表。

## 加速中國大陸地區的存取速度

Cloudflare 的預設入口是 Anycast，路由由 BGP 決定，對中國境內三大電信業者不總是友善。同一個網站，電信可能很快，中國移動在晚間尖峰時段可能會繞路並丟包。我的做法是優選 CNAME：將網域名稱 CNAME 到一個會持續測速並更新解析結果的目標網域名稱。

進站後的速度靠快取分層，規則依內容的變動頻率決定：
- 含內容雜湊的 CSS／JS／字型：快取一年
- HTML：`no-cache`，每次都要重新驗證，確保使用的是最新的程式碼
- 留言、統計這類動態 API：邊緣快取 15 秒，寫入請求一律 `no-store`。
- GitHub 熱力圖快取 6 小時，WakaTime 快取 15 分鐘。

## Automated Pipeline Workflow
GitHub Actions handles all checks, asset processing, and deployment, automatically syncing everything to Cloudflare.
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[本地 Git Push] --> B[GitHub Actions]
  B --> C[自动化校验 / 测试]
  B --> D[站点与资源构建]
  B --> E[部署到 Cloudflare]
```

1. **Local Push**: Push Markdown content to the GitHub repository via Git.
2. **CI Trigger**: GitHub Actions Capture`push`event and start the build container.
3. **Automation Workflow**: Run content checks, static asset builds, and SSR artifact packaging sequentially.
4. **Cloudflare Deployment**: Use Cloudflare Wrangler to update the live service directly.

## GitHub Actions Configuration

Create it in the repository root.`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:

```yaml
name: Deploy to Cloudflare

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run checks
        run: npm test

      - name: Build and deploy
        run: npm run deploy
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
```

In the GitHub repository settings,`Secrets and variables -> Actions`Add`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`and`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.

description: At events like Robocon, where interference is abundant and network conditions are complex, use on-site spectrum scans to strike an appropriate balance between router channels and bandwidth

tags:

## Introduction

At robotics competitions such as Robocon, network conditions are often extremely complex.

At the time, my router was using its factory-default 80 MHz bandwidth, which happened to fall in the most crowded part of the spectrum. This caused severe stuttering in WebRTC video streams, with latency at one point rising above 1 second.

A scan of the wireless environment at the venue found 88 Wi-Fi signals actively transmitting:

![Spectrum scan at the competition](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20261025165234244.png)

The scan results show that a large number of devices were clustered in the same channel and bandwidth ranges. Even without knowing the underlying principles of radio communications, we can intuitively see that too many cars on the same lane cause a traffic jam. Wi-Fi is no different: choosing a lane with fewer cars should get you there faster. And that’s exactly what happened. Simply switching the router to a suitable bandwidth and channel can greatly improve Wi-Fi stability and speed.

Here, I want to start from the underlying principles of radio communications and analyze why Wi-Fi stutters. This is also a set of study notes for my own learning about communications.

---

## Why Does Wi-Fi Stutter?

### 1. Channel Contention and Backoff (CSMA/CA)
Wi-Fi uses the half-duplex CSMA/CA mechanism. Before sending data, a device must perform carrier sensing.

When it detects an electromagnetic signal on the same frequency above a threshold (usually $-62 \text{ dBm} \sim -82 \text{ dBm}$), the device considers the channel busy and is forced to back off for a random period. When dozens of devices take turns competing for access, packets build up in queues, causing noticeable network latency and jitter.

### 2. Probability of Conflicts with Multiple Bound Channels
Home routers typically come with a factory-default bandwidth of 80 MHz, created by bonding 4 consecutive, independent 20 MHz channels (see [Bandwidth and Channel Bonding](#频宽与信道绑定)). Most phones also hard-code their 5 GHz hotspots to channel 149 or 153.

To send an 80 MHz packet, all 4 of the bonded 20 MHz channels must be idle at the same time.

Let $p$ be the probability that a single channel is occupied by nearby devices. Then the combined probability of successfully sending a packet over 80 MHz is only $(1-p)^4$. In a crowded Wi-Fi environment, the probability that all 4 channels are idle at once approaches zero.

### 3. Strong Co-Channel Interference and Modulation Downgrade
The stronger the interference signals nearby, the lower the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (see [Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR)](#信干噪比-sinr)).

According to Shannon’s theorem (see [Shannon’s Theorem](#香农定理)), channel capacity in a dense environment drops sharply as $\text{SINR}$ falls. The high data rates advertised for Wi-Fi 6 rely on 1024-QAM modulation, which requires $\text{SINR} \ge 35 \text{ dB}$ (see [QAM Modulation](#qam-调制)).

When $\text{SINR}$ falls below the threshold, the wireless chip can only automatically fall back to a lower-order modulation scheme, causing a dramatic drop in transmission bandwidth.

---

## Solution: Balancing Channels and Bandwidth On-Site

### 1. Reduce Bandwidth to Improve the Baseline Resistance to Interference
Blindly choosing higher bandwidth in a high-interference environment can backfire. According to the thermal noise formula (see [Thermal Noise Floor Formula](#热噪声底噪公式)), increasing bandwidth from 20 MHz to 80 MHz physically raises the background noise floor by:

$$\Delta N = 10 \log_{10}(4) \approx 6 \text{ dB}$$

Doubling the bandwidth physically raises the signal-to-noise threshold required by the receiving device, significantly reducing its overall resistance to interference.

### 2. Spectrum Scanning and Avoidance
In a complex network environment, first use a spectrum scanning tool to collect information about nearby signals:
- Received signal strength (RSSI)
- Operating channel
- Operating bandwidth

The core principle for choosing a channel is to avoid crowded channels and interference sources transmitting at high power. In general, you should proactively avoid frequency ranges occupied by APs with signal strengths above $-60 \text{ dBm}$.

### 3. On-Site Tuning in Practice
An analysis of the scan results above shows that the default 80 MHz bandwidth range was heavily congested. By contrast, channel 165 and channels 52 through 64 were not only clear, but also free of high-power interference signals.

In mainland China, channels 52 through 64 are in the DFS (Dynamic Frequency Selection) band. Since most phone hotspots lack radar avoidance certification, regulations prevent them from transmitting hotspots in this band at the system level. As a result, this range rarely experiences interference from hotspots.

Channel 165 is suitable for operation at 20 MHz bandwidth, sacrificing peak speed in exchange for very high transmission stability.

At the time, I switched to channels 52 and 56, with the bandwidth set to 40 MHz. As soon as the change was complete, the WebRTC video stream returned to smooth playback, latency dropped to normal levels, and interruptions disappeared entirely.

---

## Appendix: Wi-Fi Fundamentals

### AP
AP stands for Access Point. It is the radio transmission hub that connects a wired local area network to wireless clients such as phones.

Home wireless routers typically integrate an AP transmitter, network routing, and switching functions.

### Frequency Bands
#### 2.4 GHz
- The frequency range is typically 2400 MHz to 2483.5 MHz.
- Lower frequency and longer wavelength provide better wall penetration, but transmission speeds are slower. Common devices include Bluetooth devices, wireless mice, and smart home devices.

#### 5 GHz
- The total available continuous spectrum spans several hundred MHz, with common bands covering 5150 to 5350 MHz and 5725 to 5850 MHz.
- Higher frequency and shorter wavelength mean greater attenuation through walls. The main advantage is very high transmission speed.

### Channel Allocation
Communication protocols divide continuous spectrum into discrete center frequencies at fixed intervals. Each designated frequency, along with the physical bandwidth it occupies, is collectively referred to as a channel.

Adjacent channel numbers are 5 MHz apart, while the Wi-Fi standard defines the physical spectrum width of a single channel as 20 MHz.

To prevent adjacent channels from overlapping in the 5 GHz band, channel numbers must be separated by 4 (for example, 36, 40, 44, and 48; or 149, 153, 157, and 161).

### Bandwidth and Channel Bonding
Common Wi-Fi bandwidths include 20 MHz, 40 MHz, 80 MHz, and 160 MHz.

#### 20 MHz
Taking 802.11ac as an example, a 20 MHz physical channel is divided into 64 subcarriers, of which 52 are effective data carriers used to carry packets.

#### 40 MHz / 80 MHz / 160 MHz
Higher bandwidths use channel bonding. For example, with 80 MHz, the radio-frequency and baseband layers combine 4 consecutive 20 MHz channels (such as 149, 153, 157, and 161). According to Shannon’s theorem, channel capacity increases as bandwidth expands.

When bonding multiple channels, the router must designate one of them as the primary channel. The router’s management frames are transmitted on the primary channel at a bandwidth of just 20 MHz, ensuring that older devices can still connect and operate normally.

### Shannon’s Theorem

$$C = B \cdot \log_2 \left( 1 + \frac{S}{N + I} \right)$$

- $C$: Maximum channel transmission rate
- $B$: Physical bandwidth
- $S$: Received power of the useful signal
- $N$: Ambient background thermal noise
- $I$: Co-channel interference power

### Thermal Noise Floor Formula

$$N = k \cdot T \cdot B \implies N \propto 10 \log_{10}(B) \quad (\text{dBm})$$

- $B$: Physical bandwidth
- $N$: Physical background thermal noise

Increase in the noise floor as bandwidth grows by a factor:

$$\Delta N = 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{B_2}{B_1}\right)$$

Every time bandwidth doubles, the background thermal noise received by the device physically increases by $3\text{ dB}$.

### Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR)

- **SNR** (signal-to-noise ratio): $\text{SNR} = \frac{S}{N}$
- **SINR** (signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio): $\text{SINR} = \frac{S}{N + I}$

$$\text{SINR}_{(\text{dB})} \approx P_{\text{自身信号}}(\text{dBm}) - P_{\text{相邻干扰}}(\text{dBm})$$

- $P_{\text{自身信号}}$: Signal strength received by the local router (RSSI)
- $P_{\text{相邻干扰}}$: Signal strength of nearby co-channel interference sources

### QAM Modulation
Traditional modulation methods use a single dimension to switch levels or reverse phase, transmitting just 1 bit at a time.

QAM modulation divides the amplitude and phase of orthogonal electromagnetic waves into a two-dimensional constellation grid. The receiver determines the grid state to decode multiple bits simultaneously.

| Modulation scheme | Data payload per carrier | Required SINR threshold |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1024-QAM (Wi-Fi 6 top tier) | 10 bit | $\ge 35 \text{ dB}$ |
| 256-QAM (Wi-Fi 5 standard) | 8 bit | $\ge 28 \text{ dB}$ |
| 64-QAM | 6 bit | $\ge 22 \text{ dB}$ |
| 16-QAM | 4 bit | $\ge 15 \text{ dB}$ |
| QPSK (fallback mode) | 2 bit | $\approx 6 \sim 10 \text{ dB}$ |

description: 透過 Cloudflare R2 物件儲存與 PicGo 建置免出口流量費的圖床，讓 Obsidian 和 Typora 在寫作時即時自動上傳。

## 方案架構

使用 Cloudflare R2 取代傳統物件儲存，作為圖床後端。

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Obsidian / Typora] -->|本地端口 36677| B[PicGo 本地服务]
  B -->|S3 API 上传| C[Cloudflare R2 Bucket]
```

1. 編輯器貼上圖片會觸發本機 PicGo 上傳。
2. PicGo 透過 S3 相容 API 將圖片推送至 R2。
3. 介面回傳 Custom Domain 連結，並自動替換圖片位址。

---
## 為什麼選擇 Cloudflare R2

都免費給你用了，還有什麼好說的？量大管飽，基本上不會超出限額，而且徹底免除出口流量費用。對中國大陸而言，唯一的缺點是如果不掛 VPN，存取速度會比較慢。

| 資源項目                  | Cloudflare R2 每月免費額度 | 超額計費單價          |
| :-------------------- | :------------------ | :-------------- |
| **儲存空間**              | 10 GB / 月           | $0.015 / GB / 月 |
| **Class A 操作（寫入/列出）** | 100 萬次 / 月          | $4.50 / 百萬次     |
| **Class B 操作（讀取/下載）** | 1000 萬次 / 月         | $0.36 / 百萬次     |
| 出口流量                  | **永久免費，無上限**        | **$0.00**       |

---
## Cloudflare R2 啟用與準備

### 先決條件
1. 登入 Cloudflare Dashboard，進入「R2 Object Storage」。
2. 綁定信用卡或 PayPal 完成帳戶驗證。在額度內不會產生費用。

description: 在 Robocon 這類干擾很多、網路環境複雜的比賽現場，根據現場頻譜掃描結果，對路由器的頻道與頻寬進行適當權衡

## 引言

在 Robocon 等機器人比賽現場，網路環境往往極度複雜。

我的路由器當時使用出廠預設的 80 MHz 頻寬，剛好落在最擁擠的頻段。這直接導致 WebRTC 視訊串流嚴重卡頓，延遲一度飆升至 1 秒以上。

在現場使用工具掃描周遭無線環境，共發現 88 個正在發射的 Wi-Fi 訊號：

![比賽現場掃頻圖](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20261025165234244.png)

從掃頻結果可以看出，大量裝置擠在相同的頻道與頻寬範圍內。在不了解無線電底層原理的情況下，憑直覺我們就能知道，一條車道上行駛的車輛多了就會塞車，Wi-Fi 也是如此；那麼選擇幾乎沒有車的車道行駛，不就會更快了嗎？事實也確實如此，我們只需要將路由器切換到合適的頻寬與頻道，就能大幅提升 Wi-Fi 的穩定性與速率。

這裡我想從無線電底層原理出發，分析 Wi-Fi 卡頓的原因，也算是我自己學習通訊相關知識的學習筆記。

---

## 為什麼 Wi-Fi 會卡頓？

### 1. 頻道搶佔與退避機制（CSMA/CA）
Wi-Fi 採用半雙工的 CSMA/CA 機制。裝置傳送資料前必須進行載波偵聽。

當偵聽到大於門檻值（通常為 $-62 \text{ dBm} \sim -82 \text{ dBm}$）的同頻電磁訊號時，裝置判定頻道忙碌並強制隨機退避。在數十台裝置交替搶佔的環境下，資料封包嚴重排隊堆積，造成明顯的網路延遲與抖動。

### 2. 多頻道綁定的機率衝突
家用路由器預設出廠頻寬為 80 MHz，由 4 個連續的 20 MHz 獨立頻道綁定而成（詳見 [頻寬與頻道綁定](#频宽与信道绑定)）。多數手機的 5 GHz 熱點也硬編碼鎖定在 149 或 153 頻道。

裝置傳送 80 MHz 資料封包的前提，是綁定的 4 個 20 MHz 頻道必須同時處於閒置狀態。

設單個頻道被周圍裝置佔用的機率為 $p$，則 80 MHz 頻寬順利傳送封包的聯合機率僅為 $(1-p)^4$。在高密度 Wi-Fi 現場，4 個頻道同時閒置的機率趨近於零。

### 3. 同頻強干擾與調變回退
周圍干擾訊號強度越高，訊號干擾雜訊比越低（詳見 [訊號干擾雜訊比 SINR](#信干噪比-sinr)）。

根據香農公式（詳見 [香農定理](#香农定理)），高密度環境下的頻道容量隨 $\text{SINR}$ 暴跌而嚴重縮水。Wi-Fi 6 宣傳的高傳輸速率依賴 1024-QAM 調變，該調變要求 $\text{SINR} \ge 35 \text{ dB}$（詳見 [QAM 調變](#qam-调制)）。

當 $\text{SINR}$ 跌破門檻時，無線晶片只能自動回退到低階調變，導致傳輸頻寬斷崖式下跌。

---

## 解決方案：現場頻道與頻寬權衡

### 1. 降低頻寬，提升抗干擾能力
在高干擾環境下盲目選擇高頻寬會適得其反。根據熱雜訊公式（詳見 [熱雜訊底噪公式](#热噪声底噪公式)），頻寬從 20 MHz 增加到 80 MHz 時，背景底噪在物理上增加：

$$\Delta N = 10 \log_{10}(4) \approx 6 \text{ dB}$$

頻寬翻倍導致裝置接收訊號的訊噪比門檻在物理上提高，整體抗干擾能力顯著下降。

### 2. 頻譜掃描與避讓原則
在複雜網路環境下，首先使用掃頻工具採集周遭訊號狀態：
- 訊號接收強度（RSSI）
- 工作頻道
- 工作頻寬

選擇頻道的核心原則：避開密集頻道並避開高發射功率的干擾源。通常需要主動避開訊號強度大於 $-60 \text{ dBm}$ 的 AP 佔用頻段。

### 3. 現場調校實戰
分析前述掃頻結果，預設的 80 MHz 頻寬範圍重疊嚴重。相反地，頻道 165 以及頻道 52 至 64 不僅空曠，而且沒有高功率干擾訊號。

在中國大陸，52 至 64 頻道屬於 DFS（Dynamic Frequency Selection）頻段。絕大多數手機熱點因缺少雷達避讓認證，系統底層受法律限制，無法在該頻段發射熱點，因此該區域極少出現熱點干擾。

頻道 165 適合以 20 MHz 頻寬運作，可以犧牲極限速率換取極高的傳輸穩定性。

當時現場選擇切換至頻道 52 與 56，對應頻寬設為 40 MHz。完成切換後，WebRTC 視訊串流立即恢復流暢，延遲降低至正常水準，斷流現象完全消除。

---

## 附錄：Wi-Fi 理論通識

### AP
AP（Access Point）的中文名稱是無線存取點。它是連接有線區域網路與無線終端（手機等）的射頻發射中樞。

家用無線路由器通常整合了 AP 發射、網路路由與交換器功能。

### 頻段
#### 2.4 GHz
- 頻率範圍通常為 2400 MHz 至 2483.5 MHz。
- 頻率低、波長長、穿牆能力強，但傳輸速度較慢。常用裝置包括藍牙、無線滑鼠及智慧家庭終端裝置。

#### 5 GHz
- 總可用連續頻譜達數百 MHz，常見頻段涵蓋 5150 至 5350 MHz 與 5725 至 5850 MHz。
- 頻率高、波長短、穿牆衰減大，主要優勢是傳輸速率極快。

### 頻道劃分
通訊協定在連續頻譜上按照固定步長劃分離散的中心頻率點，各個標定頻率及其所佔用的實體頻寬統稱為頻道。

相鄰頻道編號間隔為 5 MHz，Wi-Fi 標準定義的單一頻道實體頻譜寬度為 20 MHz。

為了在 5 GHz 頻段內實現相鄰頻道互不重疊，頻道號碼之間需相隔 4 個單位（如 36、40、44、48 與 149、153、157、161）。

### 頻寬與頻道綁定
常見 Wi-Fi 頻寬包含 20 MHz、40 MHz、80 MHz 與 160 MHz。

#### 20 MHz
以 802.11ac 為例，20 MHz 實體頻道劃分為 64 個子載波，其中包含 52 個負責承載資料封包的有效資料載波。

#### 40 MHz / 80 MHz / 160 MHz
高頻寬採用頻道綁定機制。以 80 MHz 為例，射頻與基頻會將 4 個連續的 20 MHz 頻道（如 149、153、157、161）在底層拼接在一起。根據香農定理，頻道容量會隨頻寬擴大而提升。

綁定多個頻道時，路由器需指定其中一個頻道作為主頻道。路由器的管理訊框僅以 20 MHz 頻寬在主頻道上發射，確保舊款裝置仍可正常相容並連線。

### 香農定理

$$C = B \cdot \log_2 \left( 1 + \frac{S}{N + I} \right)$$

- $C$：頻道極限傳輸速率
- $B$：實體頻寬
- $S$：接收有用訊號功率
- $N$：環境背景熱雜訊
- $I$：同頻干擾功率

### 熱雜訊底噪公式

$$N = k \cdot T \cdot B \implies N \propto 10 \log_{10}(B) \quad (\text{dBm})$$

- $B$：實體頻寬
- $N$：實體背景熱雜訊

頻寬成倍增加時的底噪升幅：

$$\Delta N = 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{B_2}{B_1}\right)$$

頻寬每翻倍一次，裝置接收到的背景熱雜訊必然在物理上增加 $3\text{ dB}$。

### 訊號干擾雜訊比 SINR

- **SNR**（訊噪比）： $\text{SNR} = \frac{S}{N}$
- **SINR**（訊號干擾雜訊比）：$\text{SINR} = \frac{S}{N + I}$

$$\text{SINR}_{(\text{dB})} \approx P_{\text{自身信号}}(\text{dBm}) - P_{\text{相邻干扰}}(\text{dBm})$$

- $P_{\text{自身信号}}$：本地路由器接收訊號強度（RSSI）
- $P_{\text{相邻干扰}}$：同頻周邊干擾源訊號強度

### QAM 調變
傳統調變方式利用單一維度切換電平或反轉相位，單次僅能傳遞 1 個 bit。

QAM 調變將正交電磁波的振幅與相位劃分為二維網格星座圖。接收端透過辨識網格狀態同時解析多個 bit。

| 調變方式 | 單載波資料負載 | 所需訊號干擾雜訊比門檻 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1024-QAM（Wi-Fi 6 最高規格） | 10 bit | $\ge 35 \text{ dB}$ |
| 256-QAM（Wi-Fi 5 標準配備） | 8 bit | $\ge 28 \text{ dB}$ |
| 64-QAM | 6 bit | $\ge 22 \text{ dB}$ |
| 16-QAM | 4 bit | $\ge 15 \text{ dB}$ |
| QPSK（最低限度回退模式） | 2 bit | $\approx 6 \sim 10 \text{ dB}$ |

頻寬翻倍導致裝置接收訊號的訊噪比門檻在物理上提高，整體抗干擾能力顯著下降。
2. 頻譜掃描與避讓原則
在複雜網路環境下，首先使用掃頻工具採集周遭訊號狀態：
訊號接收強度（RSSI）
工作頻道
工作頻寬
選擇頻道的核心原則：避開密集頻道並避開高發射功率的干擾源。通常需要主動避開訊號強度大於 $-60 \text{ dBm}$ 的 AP 佔用頻段。
3. 現場調校實戰
分析前述掃頻結果，預設的 80 MHz 頻寬範圍重疊嚴重。相反地，頻道 165 以及頻道 52 至 64 不僅空曠，而且沒有高功率干擾訊號。
在中國大陸，52 至 64 頻道屬於 DFS（Dynamic Frequency Selection）頻段。絕大多數手機熱點因缺少雷達避讓認證，系統底層受法律限制，無法在該頻段發射熱點，因此該區域極少出現熱點干擾。
頻道 165 適合以 20 MHz 頻寬運作，可以犧牲極限速率換取極高的傳輸穩定性。
當時現場選擇切換至頻道 52 與 56，對應頻寬設為 40 MHz。完成切換後，WebRTC 視訊串流立即恢復流暢，延遲降低至正常水準，斷流現象完全消除。

AP
AP（Access Point）的中文名稱是無線存取點。它是連接有線區域網路與無線終端（手機等）的射頻發射中樞。
家用無線路由器通常整合了 AP 發射、網路路由與交換器功能。
頻段
2.4 GHz
頻率範圍通常為 2400 MHz 至 2483.5 MHz。
頻率低、波長長、穿牆能力強，但傳輸速度較慢。常用裝置包括藍牙、無線滑鼠及智慧家庭終端裝置。
5 GHz
總可用連續頻譜達數百 MHz，常見頻段涵蓋 5150 至 5350 MHz 與 5725 至 5850 MHz。
頻率高、波長短、穿牆衰減大，主要優勢是傳輸速率極快。
頻道劃分
通訊協定在連續頻譜上按照固定步長劃分離散的中心頻率點，各個標定頻率及其所佔用的實體頻寬統稱為頻道。
相鄰頻道編號間隔為 5 MHz，Wi-Fi 標準定義的單一頻道實體頻譜寬度為 20 MHz。
為了在 5 GHz 頻段內實現相鄰頻道互不重疊，頻道號碼之間需相隔 4 個單位（如 36、40、44、48 與 149、153、157、161）。
常見 Wi-Fi 頻寬包含 20 MHz、40 MHz、80 MHz 與 160 MHz。
20 MHz
以 802.11ac 為例，20 MHz 實體頻道劃分為 64 個子載波，其中包含 52 個負責承載資料封包的有效資料載波。
40 MHz / 80 MHz / 160 MHz
高頻寬採用頻道綁定機制。以 80 MHz 為例，射頻與基頻會將 4 個連續的 20 MHz 頻道（如 149、153、157、161）在底層拼接在一起。根據香農定理，頻道容量會隨頻寬擴大而提升。
綁定多個頻道時，路由器需指定其中一個頻道作為主頻道。路由器的管理訊框僅以 20 MHz 頻寬在主頻道上發射，確保舊款裝置仍可正常相容並連線。

---
title: Build a Free Image Host with Cloudflare R2 + PicGo
description: Build an image host with no egress traffic fees based on Cloudflare R2 object storage and PicGo, enabling instant automatic uploads while writing in Obsidian and Typora.
tags:
  - cloudflare
  - freebie
  - image hosting
createdAt: 2026-10-25
published: true
slug: 20261025-01
---
## Architecture

Use Cloudflare R2 instead of traditional object storage as the backend for your image host.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Obsidian / Typora] -->|本地端口 36677| B[PicGo 本地服务]
  B -->|S3 API 上传| C[Cloudflare R2 Bucket]
```

1. Pasting an image in the editor triggers a local PicGo upload.
2. PicGo pushes the image to R2 through an S3-compatible API.
3. The API returns a Custom Domain link and automatically replaces the image address.

---
## Why Choose Cloudflare R2

Since it’s free, what more is there to say? The allowances are generous, and you basically won’t exceed them. It also completely eliminates egress traffic fees. For mainland China, the only drawback is that access is relatively slow without a VPN.

| Resource item                  | Cloudflare R2 free monthly allowance | Overage unit price          |
| :-------------------- | :------------------ | :-------------- |
| **Storage space**              | 10 GB / month           | $0.015 / GB / month |
| **Class A operations (writes/listing)** | 1 million operations / month          | $4.50 / million operations     |
| **Class B operations (reads/downloads)** | 10 million operations / month         | $0.36 / million operations     |
| Egress traffic                  | **Free forever, with no limit**        | **$0.00**       |

---
## Setting Up and Preparing Cloudflare R2

### Prerequisites
1. Log in to the Cloudflare Dashboard and open “R2 Object Storage”.
2. Link a credit card or PayPal to complete account verification. No charges will be incurred within the allowance.
> If you don’t have a card, try the second-hand marketplace—you can get one for under 10 RMB.

### Manual Web Configuration
1. **Create a Bucket**: On the R2 page, click “Create bucket”, enter a name, and set Location to Automatic.
2. **Bind a public Custom Domain**: Go to Bucket -> “Settings” -> “Public Access” -> click “Connect Domain”, then enter a subdomain (for example, `img.yourdomain.com`).
3. **Get API credentials**:
   - **Account ID**: On the bottom right of the R2 overview page, click “Account Details” and copy it directly.
   - **Access Key ID and Secret Access Key**:
	  1. Click “Manage API Tokens” below “Account Details” to open the token page.
	  2. Click “Create Account API token”.
	  3. Select “Object Read & Write” under Permissions, and specify a Bucket if needed.
	  4. Click to create it, then immediately copy and save the `Access Key ID` and `Secret Access Key` on the **final success page**.
  > **Note**: `Secret Access Key` is displayed only once, when it is successfully generated. If you did not save the key for a previously created Token, it cannot be viewed again. You must click “Create Account API token” again to generate a new key.

### Agent
Creating a Bucket and binding a Custom Domain can also be done by an agent through the Wrangler CLI. You only need to run Wrangler oauth to link your own Cloudflare account.

## PicGo Client Configuration

### 1. Install the Plugin
1. Open PicGo and go to “Plugin Settings”.
2. Search for and install `picgo-plugin-cloudflare-r2`.

### 2. Configure the Parameters
Go to “Image Hosting Settings” -> “Cloudflare R2” and fill in the following configuration items:

| **Account ID**      | View it at the bottom right of the R2 overview page      |
| :------------------ | :--------------- |
| **AccessKey ID**    | Generated API Token    |
| **SecretAccessKey** | Generated API Token    |
| **Bucket name**           | Created R2 Bucket    |
| **Storage path (optional)**        | Specify directory levels as needed         |
| **Custom domain**           | R2 Custom Domain |

---

## Automatic, Seamless Upload in Editors

### Obsidian Configuration
Use local PicGo to automatically upload pasted images to the image host and replace their paths:
1. Make sure PicGo is running.
2. In Obsidian’s “Third-party plugins”, search for and install `Image auto upload Plugin`.
3. Configure the plugin to use the PicGo upload service.
4. Paste or drag an image directly into Obsidian. It will be silently uploaded to R2 in the background, and the local path in the document will be automatically replaced with a remote image-hosting link.

### Typora Configuration
Typora natively supports using the PicGo client:
1. Open Typora and go to “Preferences” -> “Images”.
2. Select “Upload images” when inserting an image.
3. Check “Apply the above rules to images in local locations” and “Apply the above rules to images in network locations”.
4. Select `PicGo (app)` as the upload service, and specify the local PicGo executable in “PicGo path”.
5. Click “Verify image upload options”. The configuration is successful once all checks pass.

![image.png](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20261025185635532.png)

---

## Cache Optimization and Anti-Abuse Strategy

Although R2 egress traffic is free, Class B read requests exceeding 10 million per month will still incur a small charge. It is recommended that you enable CDN edge caching and protection.

In the Cloudflare Dashboard, go to your domain’s “Caching” -> “Cache Rules” and add a rule:
- **Match condition**: `Hostname equals img.yourdomain.com`
- **Edge Cache TTL**: Override the origin and set it to 1 year (31536000 seconds)
- **Browser Cache TTL**: Set it to 1 year

All high-traffic images will be cached by Cloudflare CDN nodes worldwide. Subsequent requests will no longer pass through to the R2 Bucket, minimizing Class B operation usage.
